title: postfix ! is rejected as the RIGHT operand of ??, which is the same operator in the other position
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Accepted Placements': 'A `!` on a Result operand MUST be accepted if and only if all five hold', condition 1 being that every enclosing node out to the nearest statement or arrow function is one of exactly seven forms. The section's own worked example: '`maybe ?? r!` // rejected — ! is the right operand', directly under '`r! ?? "fallback"` // accepted'. This is the second of the two consequences the section says are 'easy to get wrong and MUST be read from the rule rather than guessed'. The right operand of `??` is conditionally evaluated, so an early return hoisted out of it would run when the authored program would not have evaluated it at all — which is exactly the evaluation-order constraint the section opens with. That section also states, normatively, that 'A rejected placement MUST be a diagnostic, never a silent lowering.' This case is one of the rows that enforces it: the silent lowering is the EASY outcome here, because TypeScript's own non-null assertion means something in this position and the emitted program would compile and run. A backend that lowered it silently would be scored `fail` for accepting and running a program the language rejects, not scored `pass` for staying quiet.
